target_customer: Large real estate portfolio owners and property managers
problem: Water damage costs portfolios huge sums; leaks are found late. AquaShield detects and localizes leaks from meter data and clamp-on sensors.
business_model: B2B SaaS plus sensors (pricing not public)
product_category: AI water leak detection for buildings

founders.name: Paul Beckers
founders.background_notes: YC page: robotics researcher at MIT. Education not stated.

founders.name: Marguerite Benoist
founders.background_notes: YC page: robotics researcher at Harvard; EPFL project lead per EPFL news.

competitors.name: Wint
competitors.what: AI water intelligence for commercial real estate
competitors.funding_then: Series B $15M January 2022, Series D $36M reported

technical_complexity.rationale: Time-series models, digital twins and graph localization on real building data; needs pilots and sensors.

defensibility.rationale: Building data could compound, but Wint and others are established.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established leak detection vendors already serve commercial portfolios; no outcome yet.

market_need_then: Company claims losses of up to hundreds of millions per year for large portfolios; MIT Facilities pilot and a German real estate pilot reported by EPFL in January 2026.

branding.brand_signature: Tagline: smoke detector for water leaks (F4 Fund listing)

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive and clear but many companies use AquaShield-like names; no external brand coverage.

outcome_analysis: AquaShield is a Spring 2026 company with no outcome yet. It began as an EPFL and MIT research project, has live pilots and a grant, and sells into a real cost problem. The risk is competition from Wint, a much better funded vendor, and the hardware and sales cycle in real estate.
notes: VCBacked reports $500K pre-seed May 2026 and Caplight shows $563K total; aggregators, unverified. A Caplight headline about a $16M Series A is unrelated or unverified and ignored. Grant amount is not stated. Venturekick page returned 503. Sources disagree on which school belongs to which founder.
